profile.reading:
OpenColo operates a data center at 3223 Kenneth Street in Santa Clara, California, in the heart of the Silicon Valley technology corridor. The facility totals 71,000 square feet of data center space, according to the operator's own published specifications.

The site is built around dual utility power feeds backed by 2,750 kilowatt (3,437 kVA) diesel generators and lithium ion battery backup, rather than the older lead acid battery strings still common at many colocation facilities. Cooling is handled with an N+1 indirect evaporative system, a design that leans on outside air and evaporative cooling instead of running mechanical chillers continuously. That approach suits the Santa Clara Valley's dry climate and is one that a number of newer California data centers have adopted to cut energy use. OpenColo describes its electrical and mechanical design as 2N+1, meaning fully redundant power and cooling paths with an additional layer of backup beyond simple redundancy.

On capacity, OpenColo's own site states 9 megawatts of total facility capacity, with an additional 4.5 megawatts described as coming soon at the time this page was researched. The operator's language does not clearly separate currently energized capacity from a near term expansion, so this page reports the figures as published rather than collapsing them into a single number.

OpenColo markets the facility to enterprise and carrier customers with a 100 percent uptime service level agreement and SOC 2 Type II certification, both self reported by the operator rather than independently verified for this page. The Santa Clara location places OpenColo inside one of the most competitive and expensive data center markets in the country, in the same general area as major carrier hotels and multi tenant campuses operated by much larger wholesale providers. Against that backdrop, OpenColo positions itself as a smaller, more flexible alternative aimed at customers who want direct access to facility staff and negotiated space rather than a highly standardized offering from a large national operator.

Public information about the building's ownership history, original construction date and any tenants that may have occupied the site before OpenColo was not found in the sources reviewed for this page, and the operator does not publish a founding date or history section describing when it began operating this specific Kenneth Street address. Prospective customers are directed to contact OpenColo directly for current availability and pricing rather than finding a public rate card.

reading.body:
OpenColo's Santa Clara facility claims a total capacity between 4.5 MW and 9 MW, with the operator's phrasing leaving ambiguous whether the higher figure represents current supply or near-term addition. The 71,000-square-foot campus sits in one of the densest metropolitan areas for data center infrastructure in California, where only 11 of 103 mapped facilities publish capacity figures at all.

The facility qualifies for SOC 2 Type II compliance and is provisioned with dual utility feeds, 2.75 MW of diesel generation, lithium-ion batteries, and N+1 indirect evaporative cooling. At assumed AI densities of 40 kW per rack, a 4.5 MW IT load would support roughly 110 racks, while 9 MW would support roughly 225 racks; neither figure places this campus among California's largest published capacity deployments relative to the 365 MW total published across the state.

This facility does not rank among California's top ten published data centers by capacity and cannot be confirmed as a material contributor to AI compute scaling in the state based on published specifications alone. The operator's capacity statement, if the 9 MW figure represents committed supply, would make Santa Clara one of 12 facilities California has published metrics for, but verification of which portion is operational would require operator clarification or independent confirmation.
